target_customer: Short-term rental hosts and professional property managers
problem: Airbnb hosts spend large amounts of time on guest messaging, cleaning and check-in logistics across several booking platforms.
business_model: B2B SaaS for property managers plus early on-the-ground management services
product_category: Property management software for short-term rentals

founders.name: Amiad Soto
founders.background_notes: Sales background per Entrepreneur (Nov 2014); twin brother of Koby Soto.

founders.name: Koby Soto
founders.role: CTO (listed as former founder on YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Early product was a hands-on service backed by messaging and scheduling software; multi-channel sync with Airbnb was needed but standard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Operations and integrations deepened over time, but early on the service was copyable and platform-dependent on Airbnb.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows Airbnb or HomeAway absorbing the wedge; Guesty integrated with them and continued to raise through 2021.

market_need_then: Founders started it after struggling to run their own Airbnb rentals; Airbnb and other online travel agencies were growing and hosts needed multi-platform booking management (TechCrunch 2017 describes this origin).

branding.name_origin: Originally SuperHost; renamed Guesty in 2014 per Wikipedia. Reason for the new name is not stated in opened sources.
branding.domain_note: Secured the exact-match guesty.com domain as part of the 2014 rebrand per a brand-guidelines write-up (secondary source).

identity.voice_and_tone: Built by hosts, trusted by industry

rebrands.why: Product-line rebrand reported by ShortTermRentalz, not opened

brand_strength.rationale: Clear name tied to guests and a recognizable PMS brand with ongoing press, but no sourced evidence of community or viral pull.

pivots.to: Software platform for hosts and managers
pivots.why: TechCrunch 2017 says the company began as hands-on management and pivoted twice to become an online management company; dates not given.

outcome_analysis: Guesty grew from a hands-on Airbnb management service into a software platform for short-term rental managers, reported profitability in 2016, and kept raising larger rounds through at least 2021 plus acquisitions such as MyVR and Your Porter App. It remains private with hundreds of employees. The rise of short-term rentals and a shift to software drove the outcome.
notes: Series D investors from a search summary (Apax, Kingfisher) only Apax recorded from Wikipedia total list. Series E (170M, Aug 2022, per YC page news item and search results) and Series F (130M, April 2024, KKR and others) were seen only in search snippets or aggregators, valuations 690M, 850M, 900M conflict; all unverified and not recorded as rounds. Series B 19.75M date cited as Aug 2018 vs April 2018 URL. Series A lead differs: TechCrunch says Buran VC, StartupIntros says Flashpoint. Series C total raised 60M per Pulse2 vs Wikipedia 110M total at a later date. No dated 2014 competitor named in opened sources (Skift paywalled); list left empty. Entity location listed as Tel Aviv in 2017 and New York on YC page.
